status.en: 10 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Juba, Rumbek and Abyei.
status.nb: 10 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Juba, Rumbek og Abyei.

summary.en: Coordinated cattle raids in Warrup state killed at least 72 people, while a drone strike on a market in Abyei killed at least 73, intensifying violence in South Sudan. President Kiir reshuffled the South Sudan Revenue Authority board, reinstating two commissioners after a cancelled order, and the Bar Association launched a roadmap to improve access to justice. The government partnered with Israel's Gilat to provide nationwide satellite internet and secured a UNESCO world-heritage nomination for the Boma-Bandingilo inscription. Governor Dollar promoted the reintegration of IDPs and returnees, and the U.S. Embassy remembered staff who died supporting South Sudanese people. 2 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Koordinerte kyrieangrep i Warrup-staten drepte minst 72 personer, mens et droneangrep på et marked i Abyei drepte minst 73, og intensiverte volden i Sør-Sudan. President Kiir omorganiserte styret i South Sudan Revenue Authority, og gjeninnsatte to kommisjonærer etter en avbrutt ordre, og Advokatforeningen lanserte en veikart for å forbedre rettstilgangen. Regjeringen inngikk partnerskap med Israels Gilat for å tilby landsdekkende satellittinternett og sikret en UNESCO-verdensarvnominasjon for Boma-Bandingilo-innskrivingen. Guvernør Dollar fremmet reintegrering av internt fordrevne og tilbakevendende, og den amerikanske ambassaden minnet om ansatte som døde mens de støttet det sørsudanske folket. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir Mayardit and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
